dimension_literal_resolution.lookup: scan info_type/info.{off,dat} sequentially (113 rows); read info_type/id.bin at matching row → it1_id (int32)
same scan as above, single pass capturing both literals → it2_id (int32)
scan company_name/name.{off,dat} (234,997 rows), keep rows where slice startswith 'Lionsgate'; collect company_name/id.bin values into std::unordered_set<int32_t> lionsgate_ids (expected ~10 ids)
scan keyword/keyword.{off,dat} (134,170 rows), match against std::unordered_set<string_view> literal set; collect keyword/id.bin values into std::unordered_set<int32_t> keyword_ids (expected ≤7 ids)

sampling_notes: Empirically measured: 533 titles satisfy (year>2000 AND title pattern); 135 movie_companies rows satisfy (Blu-ray note AND Lionsgate company); intersect of these two seed sets is expected to be very small (≤ few rows). Strategy: drive on the smaller mc-seed set, then validate with title filter, then probe all other facts per surviving movie_id.

join_order.notes: Parallel morsel scan over 2,609,129 movie_companies rows. For each row r: test memmem(note, '(Blu-ray)') AND lionsgate_ids.count(company_id[r]); if both true, insert movie_id[r] into a std::unordered_set<int32_t> seed_movie_ids (merge per-thread sets at end). Expected |seed_movie_ids| ≈ 100.

join_order.build: title (filtered: year>2000 AND title pattern AND id ∈ seed_movie_ids)
join_order.notes: For each v in seed_movie_ids: row = title__id__pos[v]; if row<0 skip; if production_year[row] <= 2000 skip; test title[row] against (contains 'Freddy' OR 'Jason') OR (startswith 'Saw'); survivors are candidate movie_ids (expected ≤ a handful). Keep a vector<int32_t> candidate_movie_ids and parallel vector<int32_t> title_rows.

For each candidate v: lo=mi_off[v], hi=mi_off[v+1]; scan rows in [lo,hi); keep rows where info_type_id[r]==it1_id AND mi_info[r] ∈ {Horror,Thriller}. If no surviving mi rows for v, skip v entirely. Capture min(mi.info) lex over surviving slices.
For each surviving v: scan mi_idx CSR range; keep rows where info_type_id[r]==it2_id. If none, skip. Capture min(mi_idx.info).
For each surviving v: scan mk CSR range; existence check that ∃ row where keyword_id[r] ∈ keyword_ids. If no match, skip v.

join_order.build: cast_info range per movie_id ⨝ name (via pk_pos)
join_order.notes: For each surviving v: scan ci CSR range; for each ci row r where ci_note[r] ∈ note_set: lookup name_row = name__id__pos[ci_person_id[r]]; if name_row<0 skip; if name_gender[name_row]!=0x6d skip; capture min(n.name) lex over surviving names. If no surviving ci row, skip v.
Capture min(t.title) lex over title slices for v that satisfied all other steps.

data_structures.aggregation: 4 thread-local std::string min accumulators (min mi.info, min mi_idx.info, min n.name, min t.title); merged with lex-min at end
